# Model Consensus Goal

Raw goal:

Use `docs/CODEX_DOCK_EXHAUSTIVE_SYNC_TEST_PLAN_2026-05-31.md` via
`$plan-implement` to implement the exhaustive sync testing harness and prove
that the relay gives the client every piece of information it needs, stays up
to date with the actual local Codex instances and sessions, does not drop or
lag client-visible data, and exercises the actual paths the client exercises.
The user later added that completion also requires a third leg: literal
`iPhone 17` simulator displayed-UI proof over time. Before building that third
leg, run `$model-consensus` with Opus 4.8 Max and GPT-5.5 X-High to design the
most elegant end-to-end-to-end harness and the invariants that must hold.

Goal brief:

Design the simulator displayed-UI proof leg for Codex Dock. The design must
use the existing repo and plan as source truth, preserve the already-built
relay/client-route harness, and add the missing end-to-end-to-end assurance
that the literal simulator UI stays complete, correct, and close to real time
over multiple samples. This is design only; do not edit repo files.

User-named inputs:

- `/Users/aelaguiz/workspace/codex-client/docs/CODEX_DOCK_EXHAUSTIVE_SYNC_TEST_PLAN_2026-05-31.md`
- `/Users/aelaguiz/workspace/codex-client/docs/CODEX_DOCK_EXHAUSTIVE_SYNC_TEST_PLAN_2026-05-31_IMPLEMENTATION_LOG.md`
- Repo root: `/Users/aelaguiz/workspace/codex-client`

Hard constraints:

- Use the normal `iPhone 17` simulator app path and relay-backed host path.
- Do not use mocks, preview rows, direct raw app-server connections, or
  transports the client does not exercise as completion proof.
- The proof must run over time; a single screenshot or one-shot UI check is not
  enough.
- Significant lag is a failure even if eventual sync succeeds.
- The design must identify exact invariants for missing data, stale displayed
  data, wrong detail data, wrong ordering/status/archive state, and lag.
- Reuse existing repo owner paths and Makefile/`rtk` flows where possible.
- Keep the solution lean; avoid a second source of truth for relay/client
  protocol comparison.
- Do not edit files in this model-consensus run.

- Lean proposed harness architecture.
- Existing repo paths and patterns to adopt.
- Exact displayed-UI invariants.
- How to observe literal simulator display state.
- How to correlate UI state to the existing relay/client-route audit report.

1	# Codex Dock Exhaustive Sync Test Plan
2	
3	Date: 2026-05-31
4	Status: Draft for audit
5	Doc type: Implementation plan
6	Owners: Amir, Codex
7	
8	Related docs:
9	
10	- `README.md`
11	- `docs/CODEX_DISK_DB_THREAD_TYPES_AND_STATE_2026-05-29.md`
12	- `docs/CODEX_APP_SERVER_THREAD_TYPES_AND_STATE_2026-05-29.md`
13	- `docs/CODEX_DOCK_CODEX_APP_SERVER_END_TO_END_AUDIT.md`
14	- `docs/CODEX_DOCK_RELAY_STATE_PARITY_WORKLOG_2026-05-30.md`
15	
16	## Direct Answer
17	
18	The repo already has a strong one-shot parity foundation in
19	`scripts/dock-relay-state-parity.mjs`, but it does not yet prove that the Dock
20	client stays in sync with the actual local Codex state over time.
21	
22	The missing piece is a long-running sync harness that keeps the Dock stream open,
23	clicks through or protocol-loads thread detail, watches real changes happen, and
24	compares all client-visible state back to local Codex storage and app-server
25	state on every pass.
26	
27	Eventual sync is not enough. If client-visible state catches up only after a
28	noticeable delay, the exhaustive plan must treat that as a failure because the
29	installed client feels stale while the lag is happening.
30	
31	This document specifies that harness and the ongoing loop. It is a plan only.
32	No implementation is included in this document.
33	
34	## Goal
35	
36	Build a repeatable sync-test mechanism that proves Codex Dock stays aligned with
37	the actual local Codex instance over time and stays close enough to real time
38	that user-visible lag is not hidden as a passing result.
39	
40	The mechanism must cover both client surfaces:
41	
42	1. The Dock/Home list: the cards, ordering, archive membership, source grouping,
43	   live status, goals, and host identity shown before opening a thread.
44	2. The click-through thread detail: the exact thread opened from a Dock row, its
45	   metadata, all historical turns, live events, server request cards, reconnect
46	   behavior, and stale/error states.
47	
48	The final proof has three legs:
49	
50	1. Codex storage and app-server truth to relay projection.
51	2. Relay projection to actual client-exercised protocol routes.
52	3. Actual simulator client display, using the `iPhone 17` simulator, so the
53	   test proves what is literally visible in the app stays complete, correct, and
54	   close to real time over time.
55	
56	The mechanism must compare four planes of truth:
57	
58	1. Local Codex durable storage under `CODEX_HOME`, including SQLite metadata,
59	   rollout JSONL session files, archived session files, goals, and spawn edges.
60	2. Raw Codex app-server behavior exposed through relay-side app-server calls,
61	   including `thread/list`, `thread/read`, `thread/turns/list`,
62	   `thread/goal/get`, `thread/loaded/list`, notifications, and server requests.
63	3. Dock relay projection behavior, including the relay SQLite projection,
64	   `dock/subscribe`, `dock/update`, `dock/resync`, reconciliation freshness,
65	   windowing, and stale-scope handling.
66	4. Swift client state and rendered simulator UI, including `DockStore`,
67	   `AppServerThreadCardStreamClient`, `ThreadDetailStore`,
68	   `ThreadDetailDataEngine`, visible `DockThreadCard` rows, detail content,
69	   stale/error states, and literal screen proof when required.
70	
71	## Non-Goals
72	
73	- Do not implement the harness in this plan.
74	- Do not make the iPhone connect directly to the raw authenticated
75	  `ws://127.0.0.1:4500` app-server for normal proof.
76	- Do not add relay runtime reads from Codex disk as a production shortcut.
77	  Disk reads are allowed for the verifier oracle only.
78	- Do not use preview rows, mocks, or scripted transports as completion evidence
79	  for physical or installed-client behavior.
80	- Do not log `OPENAI_API_KEY`, bearer tokens, base64 audio, raw audio bytes,
81	  prompt text, transcript text, or full JSON-RPC payloads.
82	- Do not claim unsupported Codex facts are verified. Unsupported facts must be
83	  named as product-contract gaps or app-server gaps.
84	
85	## Current State
86	
87	The current parity harness already compares several important surfaces:
88	
89	- Local SQLite thread metadata.
90	- Goal rows.
91	- Spawn edges.
92	- Rollout session metadata.
93	- Relay `relay/state/snapshot`.
94	- Dock `dock/subscribe`.
95	- Direct `thread/read` probes.
96	- Search probes.
97	
98	Important evidence:
99	
100	- `scripts/dock-relay-state-parity.mjs:127` defines `--exhaustive`,
101	  `--include-thread-reads`, `--include-turns`, `--include-goals`,
102	  `--include-loaded`, the opt-out `--no-dock-subscribe`, and `--fail-on-diff`.
103	- `scripts/dock-relay-state-parity.mjs:2740` takes one-shot relay and Dock
104	  snapshots.
105	- `scripts/dock-relay-state-parity.mjs:3149` builds the report from SQLite,
106	  goals, relay snapshot, Dock subscribe, SQLite-after, goals-after, and spawn
107	  edges.
108	- `scripts/dock-relay-state-parity.mjs:2121` compares Dock ordering against
109	  app-server active all-source order.
110	- `scripts/dock-relay-state-parity.mjs:2245` compares Dock card set,
111	  duplicates, archive extras, windows, order, and status.
112	- `scripts/dock-relay-state-parity.mjs:2528` documents blind spots.
113	- `scripts/dock-relay-state-parity.mjs:2662` defines the completion boundary.
114	
115	That foundation is not sufficient by itself because it is mostly a one-shot
116	snapshot comparison. It does not yet prove these over-time behaviors:
117	
118	- A long-lived `dock/subscribe` stream stays correct across many
119	  reconciliations.
120	- `dock/update` deltas stay gap-free and are correctly resynced after sequence
121	  breaks.
122	- Relay stale rows are retained only while a source refresh is incomplete and
123	  removed after a complete refresh proves they are gone.
124	- Swift `DockStore` state keeps matching the relay projection across many
125	  updates.
126	- A real Dock row click opens the exact matching thread detail.
127	- The detail store cannot drop live events between historical read, turn
128	  pagination, and `thread/resume`.
129	- Server requests that matter to the user are visible as both timeline events
130	  and request cards.
131	- Reconnect and foreground rehydrate restore truth before declaring `.live`.
132	
133	## Existing Architecture Evidence
134	
135	### Storage Truth
136	
137	Durable local Codex state exists in `CODEX_HOME`.
138	
139	The verifier must use these storage sources:
140	
141	- `state_5.sqlite.threads`: indexed thread metadata mirror.
142	- `state_5.sqlite.thread_spawn_edges`: normalized parent-child spawn tree.
143	- `goals_1.sqlite.thread_goals`: current persisted goal state.
144	- `$CODEX_HOME/sessions/**/*.jsonl`: rollout session history.
145	- `$CODEX_HOME/archived_sessions/**/*.jsonl`: archived rollout session history.
146	- `session_index.jsonl`: append-only name sidecar.
147	
148	Known storage limits:
149	
150	- `state_5.sqlite.threads` does not expose every live app-server fact.
151	- It does not contain an ordinary normalized turn table.
152	- It does not expose `forked_from_id` or a live app-server `session_id`.
153	- Goal storage exposes goal rows, but app-server `thread/goal/get` does not
154	  expose `goal_id`.
155	
156	### App-Server Truth
157	
158	The app-server is the bridge between local Codex storage and live process state.
159	
160	The verifier must use these app-server surfaces through the Dock relay:
161	
162	- `thread/list`
163	- `thread/read`
164	- `thread/turns/list`
165	- `thread/goal/get`
166	- `thread/loaded/list`
167	- `thread/resume`
168	- app-server notifications
169	- server requests
170	
171	Known app-server limits:
172	
173	- There is no single authoritative thread-type field. The verifier must combine
174	  `Thread.source`, `Thread.threadSource`, `Thread.status`,
175	  `thread/loaded/list`, `thread/goal/get`, and notification data.
176	- `thread/list` is persisted history plus process-local status overlay, not a
177	  global live index.
178	- `thread/search` is term-bound and cannot be used as exhaustive enumeration.
179	- No current API gives a single atomic snapshot ID across `thread/list`,
180	  `thread/read`, `thread/turns/list`, `thread/goal/get`, SQLite, and
181	  `dock/subscribe`.
182	
183	### Relay Truth
184	
185	The relay serves the client-facing stream.
186	
187	Important relay evidence:
188	
189	- `scripts/dock-relay-state-store.mjs:69` identifies the relay-owned projection
190	  while Codex durable state remains the source of truth.
191	- `scripts/dock-relay-state-engine.mjs:79` starts the periodic reconciler.
192	- `scripts/dock-relay-constants.mjs:35` sets
193	  `RELAY_STATE_RECONCILE_INTERVAL_MS = 30_000`.
194	- `scripts/dock-relay-state-engine.mjs:219` drains live leases, active
195	  all-source rows, and default interactive rows.
196	- `scripts/dock-relay-state-snapshot.mjs:145` drains paged `thread/list`.
197	- `scripts/dock-relay-state-store.mjs:508` deletes missing rows only after a
198	  complete refresh.
199	- `scripts/dock-relay-state-engine.mjs:284` keeps last good rows when refresh
200	  fails and marks scopes stale.
201	- `scripts/dock-relay-state-views.mjs:273` overlays live status without changing
202	  stored Codex order.
203	- `scripts/dock-relay-state-engine.mjs:609` abandons partial catch-up if store
204	  sequence changes mid-catchup.
205	
206	### Swift Client Truth
207	
208	The Swift app consumes relay state.
209	
210	Important Dock list evidence:
211	
212	- `CodexDock/State/AppServerThreadCardStreamClient.swift:19` connects to the
213	  Dock relay without a raw bearer token.
214	- `CodexDock/State/AppServerThreadCardStreamClient.swift:65` subscribes with
215	  `dock/subscribe`.
216	- `CodexDock/State/AppServerThreadCardStreamClient.swift:95` handles
217	  `dock/update` and `dock/resync`.
218	- `CodexDock/State/DockStore.swift:295` opens a stream per host.
219	- `CodexDock/State/DockStore.swift:364` handles incompatible updates by
220	  resyncing.
221	- `CodexDock/State/DockStore.swift:467` publishes host snapshots to the UI.
222	
223	Important thread detail evidence:
224	
225	- `CodexDock/State/ThreadDetailStore.swift:245` creates a detail session.
226	- `CodexDock/State/ThreadDetailStore.swift:249` connects and starts
227	  observation.
228	- `CodexDock/State/ThreadDetailStore.swift:556` calls
229	  `thread/read(includeTurns: false)`.
230	- `CodexDock/State/ThreadDetailStore.swift:568` drains `thread/turns/list`
231	  pages.
232	- `CodexDock/State/ThreadDetailStore.swift:606` calls
233	  `thread/resume(excludeTurns: true)`.
234	- `CodexDock/State/ThreadDetailStore.swift:611` publishes `.live` after resume.
235	- `CodexDock/State/ThreadDetailStore.swift:628` rehydrates after reconnect.
236	- `CodexDock/State/ThreadDetailStore.swift:689` applies thread notifications.
237	- `CodexDock/State/ThreadDetailStore.swift:711` applies server requests.
238	- `CodexDock/ThreadDetail/ThreadDetailDataEngine.swift:47` merges thread
239	  notifications.
240	- `CodexDock/ThreadDetail/ThreadDetailDataEngine.swift:62` merges server
241	  requests.
242	- `CodexDock/ThreadDetail/ThreadDetailDataEngine.swift:138` normalizes client
243	  presentation with `ThreadEventDisplayOrder.newestFirst`.
244	
245	## Definition Of Fully In Sync
246	
247	The harness must define sync in user-visible terms.
248	
249	### Dock/Home Sync
250	
251	For every app-server-listable, stable Codex thread, the Dock client must show
252	exactly one matching card in the expected host and source scope.
253	
254	A card is matching only when these fields agree with the selected oracle:
255	
256	- thread id
257	- source and thread source
258	- archive membership
259	- title
260	- preview, when Codex exposes preview data
261	- model provider and model, when exposed
262	- current working directory
263	- CLI version, when exposed
264	- timestamps used for ordering
265	- parent or spawn relationship, when exposed
266	- goal status, when exposed
267	- live status
268	- error or offline state
269	- host identity
270	
271	Ordering is matching only when:
272	
273	- the Dock order equals the app-server active all-source order for stable rows,
274	  or
275	- the report classifies a timestamp movement between before/after snapshots and
276	  proves the movement explains the ordering difference.
277	
278	The Dock list is not in sync when:
279	
280	- a stable expected card is missing;
281	- a card is duplicated;
282	- a non-archived row appears in the archived view or an archived row appears in
283	  the active view;
284	- a card belongs to a different host;
285	- a stale relay row is shown as fresh after a complete source refresh omitted it;
286	- live status stays present after the live lease expires;
287	- `DockStore` believes a stream is fresh while the relay reports a stale or
288	  incomplete source scope.
289	
290	### Thread Detail Sync
291	
292	Clicking a Dock row must open the exact same thread id from the same host.
293	
294	The detail view is matching only when:
295	
296	- `thread/read(includeTurns: false)` returns metadata for that thread id;
297	- all `thread/turns/list` pages are drained without duplicate turn ids or
298	  repeated cursors;
299	- client presentation is newest-first, matching
300	  `ThreadEventDisplayOrder.newestFirst`; the verifier may request app-server
301	  turns with `--turn-sort-direction desc`, but the final client order must be
302	  compared against the client presentation order;
303	- all turns exposed by app-server appear in client state;
304	- live notifications after the chosen boundary are applied exactly once;
305	- complete live snapshots replace partial events correctly;
306	- server requests after the chosen boundary appear as timeline events and
307	  request cards;
308	- resolved server request notifications update the matching request card;
309	- reconnect and foreground rehydrate reload history before declaring `.live`;
310	- `.live` is published only after read, turn drain, and
311	  `thread/resume(excludeTurns: true)` succeed.
312	
313	The detail view is not in sync when:
314	
315	- the opened detail thread id differs from the Dock row thread id;
316	- a historical turn page is skipped;
317	- a repeated cursor is accepted;
318	- a live event is dropped during initial load;
319	- a live event is applied twice;
320	- a notification for another thread mutates the detail view;
321	- a server request is visible in app-server but absent from the UI state;
322	- reconnect publishes `.live` using old state without a fresh compact read;
323	- resume fails but the UI reports the thread as live.
324	
325	### Time-Based Sync
326	
327	One snapshot is not enough. The harness must prove convergence over time, and it
328	must prove that convergence happens within an explicit near-real-time budget.
329	The test cannot pass merely because the client eventually reaches the right
330	state.
331	
332	For each scenario, the harness must record:
333	
334	- `t0`: before the local Codex or app-server change.
335	- `t_change`: when the change is made or observed by app-server.
336	- `t_relay_seen`: when the relay projection first includes the change.
337	- `t_dock_seen`: when the long-lived `dock/subscribe` stream or Swift
338	  `DockStore` first includes the change.
339	- `t_detail_seen`: when the detail probe or Swift `ThreadDetailStore` first
340	  includes the change.
341	- `t_stable`: when at least two consecutive checks agree across all required
342	  planes.
343	
344	For each scenario, the harness must also compute and report:
345	
346	- `lag_change_to_relay_ms`: `t_relay_seen - t_change`.
347	- `lag_relay_to_dock_ms`: `t_dock_seen - t_relay_seen`.
348	- `lag_dock_to_detail_ms`: `t_detail_seen - t_dock_seen`, when detail is in
349	  scope.
350	- `lag_change_to_stable_ms`: `t_stable - t_change`.
351	
352	The default convergence budget is:
353	
354	- one successful relay reconciliation interval for relay projection changes;
355	- `dock/update` delivery within the configured client-visible lag budget after
356	  relay projection changes;
357	- one explicit resync cycle after a detected sequence gap or schema mismatch;
358	- one complete detail rehydrate after reconnect or foreground.
359	
360	The default client-visible lag budget for the Dock stream is 2,000 ms, exposed
361	by the audit tool as `--max-stream-lag-ms`. A stricter run may lower this
362	budget. Any run that exceeds the configured lag budget must fail even if a later
363	sample eventually matches.
364	
365	If a source scope is stale or incomplete, the client may show stale data only
366	when the stale or partial state is explicit in the report and client state. It
367	must not be counted as a fresh pass.
368	
369	### Unsupported Facts
370	
371	Unsupported facts cannot be silently ignored.
372	
373	The report must classify each unsupported fact as one of:
374	
375	- `outside_app_server_contract`: local storage has the fact but no app-server API
376	  exposes it.
377	- `outside_client_contract`: app-server exposes the fact but the Dock client is
378	  not intended to show it.
379	- `product_gap`: the user-visible contract needs the fact, but the app-server or
380	  client cannot currently prove it.
381	
382	The harness must fail final completion if a `product_gap` exists for any
383	client-required field.
384	
385	## Initial Tool Build
386	
387	The first implementation phase should build a canonical audit tool, not a
388	parallel copy of the existing parity logic.
389	
390	### Planned Tool
391	
392	Add a new planned script:
393	
394	```text
395	scripts/dock-relay-sync-audit.mjs
396	```
397	
398	This script should orchestrate the complete sync audit. It should reuse or
399	factor logic from:
400	
401	- `scripts/dock-relay-state-parity.mjs`
402	- `scripts/dock-relay-state-snapshot.mjs`
403	- `scripts/dock-relay-state-engine.mjs`
404	- `scripts/dock-relay-state-store.mjs`
405	- `scripts/dock-relay-state-views.mjs`
406	- `scripts/dock-relay-thread-fidelity.mjs`
407	
408	The existing `scripts/dock-relay-state-parity.mjs` should become either:
409	
410	- a wrapper around shared collector and comparator modules, or
411	- the source module that exports collectors and comparators for the new audit
412	  script.
413	
414	Do not create a second definition of storage truth, relay truth, source-scope
415	truth, or diff classification.
416	
417	### Planned CLI Shape
418	
419	One-shot exhaustive audit:
420	
421	```bash
422	rtk node scripts/dock-relay-sync-audit.mjs \
423	  --relay-url ws://127.0.0.1:4510 \
424	  --mode one-shot \
425	  --exhaustive \
426	  --detail all \
427	  --json-out /tmp/codex-client/sync-audit/one-shot.json \
428	  --summary-out /tmp/codex-client/sync-audit/one-shot.md \
429	  --fail-on-diff
430	```
431	
432	Long-running soak audit:
433	
434	```bash
435	rtk node scripts/dock-relay-sync-audit.mjs \
436	  --relay-url ws://127.0.0.1:4510 \
437	  --mode soak \
438	  --duration-ms 900000 \
439	  --sample-interval-ms 30000 \

479	### Tool Components
480	
481	#### 1. Storage Oracle
482	
483	The storage oracle reads local Codex durable state before and after each audit
484	sample.
485	
486	Inputs:
487	
488	- `CODEX_HOME`
489	- `state_5.sqlite`
490	- `goals_1.sqlite`
491	- rollout session files
492	- archived rollout session files
493	- `session_index.jsonl`
494	
495	Outputs:
496	
497	- stable thread rows
498	- archived thread rows
499	- previewless rows
500	- thread metadata
501	- goal rows
502	- spawn edges
503	- rollout `session_meta`
504	- storage movement between before and after samples
505	- unsupported fields
506	
507	Rules:
508	
509	- Treat storage as durable truth, not live truth.
510	- Treat movement between before/after snapshots as a classification input, not a
511	  pass by default.
512	- Do not fail on previewless rows being absent from `thread/list` unless the
513	  product contract requires them in the Dock.
514	- Do fail if an app-server-listable stable row is absent from Dock after the
515	  convergence budget.
516	- Never log prompt text or full JSONL payloads.
517	
518	#### 2. App-Server Oracle
519	
520	The app-server oracle collects the raw Codex app-server surface through relay
521	helpers.
522	
523	Inputs:
524	
525	- `relay/state/snapshot`
526	- direct routed `thread/read`
527	- direct history `thread/read`
528	- `thread/turns/list`
529	- `thread/goal/get`
530	- `thread/loaded/list`
531	
532	Outputs:
533	
534	- app-server-listable thread set
535	- source-scope membership
536	- archive membership
537	- read metadata
538	- turns
539	- goal state
540	- loaded live state
541	- routed-vs-history conflicts
542	- incomplete scopes
543	- repeated cursor failures
544	
545	Rules:
546	
547	- `--exhaustive` must imply thread reads, turns, goals, loaded state,
548	  Dock subscribe, and full enough turn evidence for the selected detail mode.
549	- A repeated cursor in `thread/turns/list` is a hard detail-read failure.
550	- A missing routed read can be acceptable only when a history read succeeds and
551	  the report classifies why routed live state is unavailable.
552	- `thread/search` cannot be used as exhaustive enumeration.
553	
554	#### 3. Relay Projection Probe
555	
556	The relay projection probe observes the relay state store and stream contract.
557	
558	Inputs:
559	
560	- `relay/state/snapshot`
561	- `dock/subscribe`
562	- `dock/update`
563	- `dock/resync`
564	- relay status metadata
565	- relay state freshness metadata
566	
567	Outputs:
568	
569	- projected card rows
570	- window slices
571	- update sequences
572	- stale scopes
573	- incomplete scopes
574	- live status overlay
575	- catch-up results
576	- resync requests
577	
578	Rules:
579	
580	- Open at least one long-lived `dock/subscribe` stream for the duration of soak
581	  mode.
582	- Record every sequence number received.
583	- Force a resync when the stream contract says to resync.
584	- Fail if a gap is not detected.
585	- Fail if a detected gap does not converge after resync.
586	- Fail if the long-lived stream takes longer than `--max-stream-lag-ms` to
587	  match a fresh client-path `dock/subscribe` view after divergence is detected.
588	- Gap injection should reuse the Swift patterns in
589	  `CodexDockTests/DockStoreStreamTests.swift` for client behavior and add a
590	  test-only Node relay stream harness if protocol-level gap injection is needed.
591	  Do not add a production-only debug endpoint for this.
592	- Fail if stale rows survive after a complete refresh that omits them.
593	- Fail if live leases do not expire from client-visible state.
594	
595	#### 4. Dock Client Probe
596	
597	The Dock client probe validates Swift-visible state.
598	
599	First implementation can start with protocol-level Dock stream proof. Final
600	completion must include Swift store proof for the same contract.
601	
602	Inputs:
603	
604	- `DockStore`
605	- `AppServerThreadCardStreamClient`
606	- simulator app state or a test harness using real relay protocol
607	
608	Outputs:
609	
610	- host snapshot rows
611	- stream health
612	- last sequence
613	- stale/offline state
614	- visible ordering
615	- selected row identity for click-through
616	
617	Rules:
618	
619	- A protocol-level pass proves relay behavior, not full Swift UI behavior.
620	- A Swift store pass is required before claiming the Dock client itself stays in
621	  sync.
622	- A simulator screenshot can support UI proof, but it cannot replace state
623	  comparison.
624	- Physical phone proof must use relay-backed host paths, not raw app-server
625	  loopback.
626	
627	#### 5. Thread Detail Probe
628	
629	The detail probe validates click-through state for selected threads.
630	
631	Inputs:
632	
633	- selected Dock row thread id and host id
634	- `thread/read(includeTurns: false)`
635	- all `thread/turns/list` pages
636	- `thread/resume(excludeTurns: true)`
637	- `session.notifications`
638	- `session.serverRequests`
639	- reconnect and foreground triggers
640	
641	Outputs:
642	
643	- opened thread id
644	- detail metadata
645	- historical turn list
646	- live event list
647	- active turn id
648	- request cards
649	- resume state
650	- reconnect state
651	
652	Rules:
653	
654	- Select detail targets from actual Dock rows, not from arbitrary ids only.
655	- Verify row thread id equals detail thread id.
656	- Verify host identity is unchanged.
657	- Verify `thread/read`, all turn pages, and `thread/resume` complete before
658	  `.live`.
659	- Record a live boundary before applying live deltas.
660	- Either prove app-server gives an atomic boundary or buffer live events until
661	  historical load completes and replay them.
662	- Follow the `ThreadDetailStore.startObservation` pattern: collect
663	  `session.notifications` and `session.serverRequests` as async streams, not as
664	  one-time polls.
665	- Fail on live event loss between observation start, history replace, turn
666	  pagination, and resume.
667	- Fail if a server request visible after the boundary is missing from the
668	  timeline or request-card state.
669	- Fail if reconnect publishes `.live` before a fresh compact read succeeds.
670	
671	#### 6. Scenario Driver
672	
673	The scenario driver creates controlled changes in an isolated Codex home.
674	
675	Modes:
676	
677	- read-only real-home audit: observes the user's current Codex home without
678	  creating or mutating threads.
679	- isolated scenario audit: creates a temporary `CODEX_HOME` under
680	  `/tmp/codex-client/...` and drives known state transitions.
681	
682	Required scenarios:
683	
684	1. Existing idle active thread appears in Dock.
685	2. Existing archived thread appears only in archived views.
686	3. New thread is created and appears within the convergence budget.
687	4. Existing thread receives a new turn and moves order correctly.
688	5. Active live thread appears as live and later expires when no longer live.
689	6. Thread is archived and disappears from active Dock after complete refresh.
690	7. Thread is unarchived and reappears in active Dock after complete refresh.
691	8. Goal state changes and matches app-server-visible goal state.
692	9. Subagent spawn edge appears where app-server and client contracts expose it.
693	10. Server request appears in detail as both event and request card.
694	11. Server request resolution updates the card.
695	12. Relay source refresh fails and stale state is explicit.
696	13. Relay source refresh recovers and stale rows are reconciled.
697	14. Stream sequence gap triggers resync and converges.
698	15. Reconnect reloads thread detail before `.live`.
699	16. Multi-host configuration keeps rows isolated by host.
700	
701	Scenario actuator contract:
702	
703	- Each scenario must declare the exact actuator used to create the state change:
704	  Codex CLI command, app-server RPC, relay test fixture, or direct isolated
705	  storage fixture.
706	- Prefer real Codex CLI or app-server flows when the goal is end-to-end
707	  behavior. Use direct storage fixtures only for storage-edge cases that cannot
708	  be produced through supported APIs.
709	- The isolated scenario runner must document how `CODEX_HOME` is pointed at the
710	  temporary directory. If `rtk make services` cannot accept that environment
711	  directly, implementation must add a Makefile-owned wrapper instead of using
712	  raw service startup commands as the normal path.
713	- Server-request scenarios must name the request source and the expected request
714	  resolution path before they can count as completion evidence.
715	
716	#### 7. Reporter
717	
718	The reporter writes sanitized machine-readable and human-readable output.
719	
720	Required outputs:
721	
722	- JSON report
723	- Markdown summary
724	- failing invariant list
725	- unsupported fact list
726	- stale or incomplete scope list
727	- movement classification
728	- event timeline
729	- selected detail target list
730	- exact commands used
731	- exact service endpoints used
732	- exact app build or relay commit when available
733	
734	Required redaction:
735	
736	- no bearer tokens
737	- no `OPENAI_API_KEY`
738	- no raw prompts
739	- no transcript text
740	- no raw audio
741	- no full JSON-RPC payloads

743	## Invariants
744	
745	Every audit report must evaluate these invariants.
746	
747	### Storage Invariants
748	
749	`S-01`: The storage oracle can open the expected `CODEX_HOME` databases and
750	session directories, or the report fails with the exact missing path.
751	
752	`S-02`: Every `state_5.sqlite.threads` row is classified as active, archived,
753	previewless, unsupported, or outside the client contract.
754	
755	`S-03`: Every rollout `session_meta` thread id is either matched to SQLite,
756	classified as archived-only, classified as previewless, or reported as a storage
757	disagreement.
758	
759	`S-04`: Every `goals_1.sqlite.thread_goals` row is matched to a thread id or
760	reported as an orphan goal.
761	
762	`S-05`: Every `thread_spawn_edges` edge references known parent and child ids or
763	is reported as a storage disagreement.
764	
765	`S-06`: Before/after storage movement is recorded and cannot silently mask a
766	client mismatch.
767	
768	### App-Server Invariants
769	
770	`A-01`: `thread/list` drains all requested source scopes without repeated
771	cursors.
772	
773	`A-02`: `relay/state/snapshot --exhaustive` includes active, archived, default
774	interactive, all-source, loaded, goals, reads, and turns for the selected audit
775	mode.
776	
777	`A-03`: Every app-server-listable stable thread maps to a storage row or a
778	clearly classified app-server-only live row.
779	
780	`A-04`: Every app-server read result agrees with list metadata for id, archive
781	state, source, thread source, cwd, model/provider, and timestamps when both
782	surfaces expose the field.
783	
784	`A-05`: Routed read and history read conflicts are reported with both values and
785	the selected canonical projection.
786	
787	`A-06`: `thread/turns/list` either drains all pages or fails the detail audit.
788	
789	`A-07`: `thread/goal/get` results agree with goal storage for all exposed goal
790	fields. Missing `goal_id` is recorded as an app-server contract limit.
791	
792	`A-08`: `thread/loaded/list` live state agrees with relay live overlay after
793	lease rules are applied.
794	
795	### Relay Projection Invariants
796	
797	`R-01`: Relay state scopes report freshness, completeness, and last successful
798	refresh time.
799	
800	`R-02`: Relay active projection includes every stable app-server active thread
801	after a successful complete refresh.
802	
803	`R-03`: Relay archived projection includes every stable app-server archived
804	thread after a successful complete refresh.
805	
806	`R-04`: Relay does not delete rows after incomplete refreshes.
807	
808	`R-05`: Relay deletes or reclassifies rows after complete refreshes prove they
809	are gone or archived.
810	
811	`R-06`: Relay order matches app-server active all-source order for stable rows,
812	except movement classified by before/after snapshots.
813	
814	`R-07`: Relay live overlay does not change stored Codex order.
815	
816	`R-08`: Relay live overlay expires stale leases.
817	
818	`R-09`: Relay catch-up windows contain no duplicate ids, skipped rows, or
819	incorrect offsets.
820	
821	`R-10`: Relay sequence gaps are detectable by clients.
822	
823	### Dock Stream Invariants
824	
825	`D-01`: `dock/subscribe` returns a complete initial window or explicitly marks
826	the relevant scope stale/incomplete.
827	
828	`D-02`: `dock/update` sequences are strictly increasing per stream.
829	
830	`D-03`: The long-lived stream receives every relay projection change after the
831	change is committed.
832	
833	`D-04`: If the stream misses a change, it emits or requires `dock/resync`.
834	
835	`D-05`: After `dock/resync`, the stream converges to the relay projection.
836	
837	`D-06`: Windowed streams preserve exact offsets, total counts, and row identity.
838	
839	`D-07`: Active and archived windows never leak rows across archive boundaries
840	after a complete refresh.
841	
842	`D-08`: Host identity in every card matches the subscribed host.
843	
844	### Swift DockStore Invariants
845	
846	`C-01`: `DockStore` opens a stream for each configured host and does not collapse
847	host state.
848	
849	`C-02`: `DockStore` publishes the same card set as `dock/subscribe` plus applied
850	updates.
851	
852	`C-03`: `DockStore` preserves update order and resyncs on incompatible updates.
853	
854	`C-04`: `DockStore` reports stale, offline, and reconnecting states instead of
855	presenting stale data as fresh.
856	
857	`C-05`: `DockStore` keeps one-host failures isolated from other hosts.
858	
859	`C-06`: Visible row order matches the relay projection for stable rows.
860	
861	### Thread Detail Invariants
862	
863	`T-01`: The selected Dock row thread id equals the opened detail thread id.
864	
865	`T-02`: The selected Dock row host equals the detail session host.
866	
867	`T-03`: Detail load calls `thread/read(includeTurns: false)`.
868	
869	`T-04`: Detail load drains every `thread/turns/list` page.
870	
871	`T-05`: Repeated turn cursors fail the load and prevent `.live`.
872	
873	`T-06`: Duplicate turn ids fail the load.
874	
875	`T-07`: Turn ordering matches the documented presentation contract.
876	
877	`T-08`: `.live` is published only after read, turns, and resume succeed.
878	
879	`T-09`: Resume failure leaves the view loaded but stale, not live.
880	
881	`T-10`: Live notifications for other thread ids do not mutate this detail state.
882	
883	`T-11`: Live partial deltas merge into the right turn/event.
884	
885	`T-12`: Complete live snapshots replace partial event state correctly.
886	
887	`T-13`: Live events emitted during initial load are either included in the
888	historical read or buffered and replayed.
889	
890	`T-14`: Server requests after the live boundary appear as timeline events.
891	
892	`T-15`: Server requests after the live boundary appear as request cards.
893	
894	`T-16`: Server request resolutions update the matching request cards.
895	
896	`T-17`: Reconnect and foreground rehydrate run a fresh compact read before
897	publishing `.live`.
898	
899	`T-18`: Rehydrate does not duplicate historical events.
900	
901	### Soak Invariants
902	
903	`K-01`: Every sampled cycle records storage before, app-server state, relay
904	state, Dock stream state, selected detail state, and storage after.
905	
906	`K-02`: Every intentional scenario mutation reaches stable agreement or fails
907	with a named invariant.
908	
909	`K-03`: At least two consecutive samples after convergence remain in agreement.
910	
911	`K-04`: Failures include first-bad timestamp, last-good timestamp, and affected
912	thread ids.
913	
914	`K-05`: A stale/incomplete source scope cannot be counted as a fresh pass.
915	
916	`K-06`: Long-running stream state is compared to fresh one-shot state on every
917	sample.

1049

1139	### Phase 1: Shared Collectors And Comparator
1140	
1141	Goal: avoid duplicate truth logic.
1142	
1143	Tasks:
1144	
1145	- Factor or export storage collectors from `dock-relay-state-parity.mjs`.
1146	- Factor or export relay snapshot collectors.
1147	- Factor or export Dock subscribe comparison logic.
1148	- Keep existing parity command behavior working.
1149	- Add a shared report model for invariant results and failure codes.
1150	
1151	Exit criteria:
1152	
1153	- Existing parity command still passes its current tests.
1154	- `rtk npm run test:relay` passes for relay changes.
1155	- New shared modules can produce the same one-shot report as the current parity
1156	  script.
1157	
1158	### Phase 2: Long-Lived Dock Stream Watcher
1159	
1160	Goal: prove the Dock stream stays aligned over time.
1161	
1162	Tasks:
1163	
1164	- Add a watcher that keeps `dock/subscribe` open.
1165	- Record every `dock/update` sequence.
1166	- Compare long-lived state to fresh relay snapshot on each sample.
1167	- Inject or simulate sequence gaps where current test helpers allow it.
1168	- Force `dock/resync` and verify convergence.
1169	- Track stale and incomplete source scopes.
1170	
1171	Exit criteria:
1172	
1173	- Long-lived stream reaches the same stable state as one-shot
1174	  `dock/subscribe`.
1175	- Sequence gaps are detected and recovered.
1176	- Stale scopes are never counted as fresh.
1177	
1178	### Phase 3: Detail Click-Through Verifier
1179	
1180	Goal: prove row-to-detail sync.
1181	
1182	Tasks:
1183	
1184	- Select detail targets from actual Dock rows.
1185	- Open detail through the same protocol path used by `ThreadDetailStore`.
1186	- Drain `thread/read` and all `thread/turns/list` pages.
1187	- Resume with `thread/resume(excludeTurns: true)`.
1188	- Keep observation open for notifications and server requests.
1189	- Prove or fix the initial-load live-event race.
1190	- Verify request cards and resolution.
1191	- Verify reconnect rehydrate.
1192	
1193	Exit criteria:
1194	
1195	- Every selected row opens the same thread id and host.
1196	- Historical turns match app-server truth.
1197	- Live events are not dropped or duplicated.
1198	- Request cards match server requests.
1199	- `.live` is never published before read, turns, and resume succeed.
1200	
1201	### Phase 4: Controlled Scenario Runner
1202	
1203	Goal: prove known transitions, not just passive current state.
1204	
1205	Tasks:
1206	
1207	- Create an isolated `CODEX_HOME` under `/tmp/codex-client/...`.
1208	- Start services against that isolated home.
1209	- Drive the required scenarios.
1210	- Record timestamps for every mutation and convergence point.
1211	- Keep reports sanitized.
1212	
1213	Exit criteria:
1214	
1215	- Required scenarios pass twice in a row.
1216	- Failures are deterministic and attached to invariant ids.
1217	- Real-home read-only audit still works separately.
1218	
1219	### Phase 5: Swift Client Proof
1220	
1221	Goal: prove the actual client state, not only relay protocol state.
1222	
1223	Tasks:
1224	
1225	- Add or extend Swift tests around `DockStore` long-lived sync.
1226	- Add or extend Swift tests around `ThreadDetailStore` row-to-detail sync.
1227	- Verify stale, offline, reconnecting, and resync UI states.
1228	- Use simulator app proof where behavior crosses store and UI boundaries.
1229	
1230	Exit criteria:
1231	
1232	- `rtk swift test --filter DockStoreTests` passes.
1233	- `rtk swift test --filter ThreadDetailStoreTests` passes.
1234	- `rtk swift test --filter AppServerClientTests` passes when JSON-RPC or DTO
1235	  behavior changes.
1236	- `rtk make app-test SIM='iPhone 17'` passes when installed UI behavior is in
1237	  scope.
1238	
1239	### Phase 6: Simulator Displayed-UI End-To-End-To-End Proof
1240	
1241	Goal: prove what is literally displayed in the simulator stays in sync over
1242	time. This is the third leg after Codex-to-relay proof and relay-to-client-route
1243	proof.
1244	
1245	This phase is required before the overall goal can be called complete. It must
1246	use the `iPhone 17` simulator and the normal relay-backed app path, not mocks,
1247	preview rows, direct raw app-server connections, or scripted transports that the
1248	client does not exercise.
1249	
1250	Before implementing this phase, run `$model-consensus` with the requested model
1251	pair, Opus 4.8 Max and GPT-5.5 X-High, to design the most elegant
1252	end-to-end-to-end harness and the invariants it must enforce. Do not start this
1253	phase until that consensus design exists and is recorded.
1254	
1255	Tasks:
1256	
1257	- Launch the app through Makefile-owned simulator flows such as
1258	  `rtk make app-test SIM='iPhone 17'` or the matching app launch target.
1259	- Configure the simulator app to use the relay-backed host path on `:4510`.
1260	- Observe the literal Dock/Home UI over time and compare displayed
1261	  `DockThreadCard` rows to the same Codex, app-server, relay, and client-route
1262	  report used by the earlier phases.
1263	- Open displayed Dock rows in the simulator and compare the literal detail UI to
1264	  `thread/read`, `thread/turns/list`, `thread/resume`, live notifications, and
1265	  server-request truth.
1266	- Measure lag all the way through the rendered UI, not only through the relay
1267	  stream. A pass requires the displayed simulator state to converge within the
1268	  configured client-visible lag budget.
1269	- Capture enough simulator evidence, such as accessibility snapshots,
1270	  screenshots, app logs, and audit timestamps, to explain the first bad visible
1271	  row, missing detail item, stale state, or lag violation.
1272	- Keep the test running over time across multiple samples. A single screenshot
1273	  or one-shot UI check is not enough.
1274	
1275	Exit criteria:
1276	
1277	- The simulator Dock list displays every client-required card exactly once,
1278	  with correct host, archive membership, status, ordering, and stale/error
1279	  state.
1280	- Opening a visible Dock row displays the same thread id and complete
1281	  client-required detail state.
1282	- The rendered UI does not miss client-required data that exists in Codex,
1283	  app-server, relay, or the client-route probe.
1284	- The rendered UI does not exceed the configured lag budget.
1285	- The simulator proof runs over time and produces a reusable report that can be
1286	  run again as a regression harness.
1287	- The `$model-consensus` design result is attached or referenced before this
1288	  phase is implemented.
1289	
1290	### Phase 7: Runbook And Continuous Loop
1291	
1292	Goal: make the harness usable repeatedly.
1293	
1294	Tasks:
1295	
1296	- Document the one-shot, soak, scenario, Swift proof, and simulator displayed-UI
1297	  proof commands in `README.md` or a dedicated runbook.
1298	- Define where reports go under `/tmp/codex-client/...`.
1299	- Add CI-safe subsets if possible.
1300	- Keep real-home audits local-only unless sanitized report artifacts are
1301	  intentionally shared.
1302	
1303	Exit criteria:
1304	
1305	- A developer can run the loop without reading source code.
1306	- The loop clearly says pass, fail, blocked, or outside-contract.
1307	- Reports preserve exact commands and exact blockers.
1308	
1309	## Completion Gate
1310	
1311	The mechanism is complete only when all of these are true:
1312	
1313	1. One-shot audit passes on a real local service stack.
1314	2. Soak audit passes across multiple reconciliation intervals.
1315	3. Controlled scenario audit passes for required transitions.
1316	4. Dock stream proof includes `dock/subscribe`, `dock/update`, and
1317	   `dock/resync`.
1318	5. No sample exceeds the configured client-visible lag budget.
1319	6. Detail proof starts from actual Dock rows and validates `thread/read`,
1320	   `thread/turns/list`, `thread/resume`, notifications, and server requests.
1321	7. Swift store tests pass for Dock list and thread detail state.
1322	8. `$model-consensus` with Opus 4.8 Max and GPT-5.5 X-High has designed the
1323	   simulator displayed-UI harness and invariant list.
1324	9. Simulator displayed-UI proof passes on `iPhone 17` and verifies the literal
1325	   app screen over time.
1326	10. Simulator displayed-UI proof uses actual client-exercised paths and fails
1327	   on missing data, stale displayed data, wrong detail data, or lag beyond the
1328	   configured budget.
1329	11. Unsupported facts are explicitly classified.
1330	12. No client-required field is classified as `product_gap`.
1331	13. Reports are sanitized and contain stable invariant ids.
1332	14. The ongoing loop has been run at least twice with the same passing result.
1333	
1334	## Open Risks
1335	
1336	### No Atomic Cross-Plane Snapshot
1337	
1338	There is no single snapshot id across storage, app-server, relay, Dock stream,
1339	and Swift client state.
1340	
1341	Mitigation:
1342	
1343	- take storage before and after;
1344	- record app-server, relay, stream, and detail timestamps;
1345	- classify movement;
1346	- require two stable samples after convergence.
1347	
1348	### Detail Initial-Load Race
1349	
1350	`ThreadDetailStore` starts observation before historical read and turn drain, but
1351	history replacement can overwrite state. A live event could be emitted during
1352	the initial load window.
1353	
1354	Mitigation:
1355	
1356	- choose and record a live boundary;
1357	- prove app-server history includes all events before the boundary, or buffer
1358	  live events until the history load completes and replay them;
1359	- add a targeted test before claiming detail sync.
1360	
1361	### Previewless Rows
1362	
1363	Storage can contain previewless rows outside current `thread/list` behavior.
1364	
1365	Mitigation:
1366	
1367	- classify previewless rows separately;
1368	- do not require Dock cards for rows outside app-server list support unless the
1369	  product contract changes.
1370	
1371	### Orphan Goals
1372	
1373	`goals_1.sqlite` can contain goal rows app-server cannot list globally.
1374	
1375	Mitigation:
1376	
1377	- compare `thread/goal/get` for known thread ids;
1378	- report orphan goals as unsupported or storage disagreement;
1379	- do not claim global goal exhaustiveness until app-server exposes it.
1380	
1381	### Historical Prompt Start And Output Schema
1382	
1383	Some historical prompt-start and output schema details are not reliably exposed
1384	through app-server APIs.
1385	
1386	Mitigation:
1387	
1388	- keep those facts out of client-required sync unless APIs expose them;
1389	- classify them as `outside_app_server_contract` when encountered.
1390	
1391	## Plan Audit Requirement
1392	
1393	Before implementation starts, this plan must pass:
1394	
1395	1. `$plan-audit` against this file and the relevant code paths.
1396	2. `$fresh-consult` using Cursor Agent `composer-2.5-fast`.
1397	
1398	Before Phase 6 starts, the simulator displayed-UI harness design must pass
1399	`$model-consensus` using Opus 4.8 Max and GPT-5.5 X-High. That consensus must
1400	define the end-to-end-to-end approach, the exact invariants, how literal
1401	simulator display state is observed, and how over-time lag is measured through
1402	the rendered client.
1403	
1404	Both reviews must agree that the plan fully defines:
1405	
1406	- the initial tool build;
1407	- the long-running over-time sync loop;
1408	- Dock/Home list comparison;
1409	- click-through thread detail comparison;
1410	- storage, app-server, relay, and Swift client truth boundaries;
1411	- unsupported facts and product gaps;
1412	- proof gates and exact commands.

# Codex Dock Exhaustive Sync Test Plan

Date: 2026-05-31
Status: Draft for audit
Doc type: Implementation plan
Owners: Amir, Codex

Related docs:

- `README.md`
- `docs/CODEX_DISK_DB_THREAD_TYPES_AND_STATE_2026-05-29.md`
- `docs/CODEX_APP_SERVER_THREAD_TYPES_AND_STATE_2026-05-29.md`
- `docs/CODEX_DOCK_CODEX_APP_SERVER_END_TO_END_AUDIT.md`
- `docs/CODEX_DOCK_RELAY_STATE_PARITY_WORKLOG_2026-05-30.md`

## Direct Answer

The repo already has a strong one-shot parity foundation in
`scripts/dock-relay-state-parity.mjs`, but it does not yet prove that the Dock
client stays in sync with the actual local Codex state over time.

The missing piece is a long-running sync harness that keeps the Dock stream open,
clicks through or protocol-loads thread detail, watches real changes happen, and
compares all client-visible state back to local Codex storage and app-server
state on every pass.

Eventual sync is not enough. If client-visible state catches up only after a
noticeable delay, the exhaustive plan must treat that as a failure because the
installed client feels stale while the lag is happening.

This document specifies that harness and the ongoing loop. It is a plan only.
No implementation is included in this document.

## Goal

Build a repeatable sync-test mechanism that proves Codex Dock stays aligned with
the actual local Codex instance over time and stays close enough to real time
that user-visible lag is not hidden as a passing result.

The mechanism must cover both client surfaces:

1. The Dock/Home list: the cards, ordering, archive membership, source grouping,
   live status, goals, and host identity shown before opening a thread.
2. The click-through thread detail: the exact thread opened from a Dock row, its
   metadata, all historical turns, live events, server request cards, reconnect
   behavior, and stale/error states.

The final proof has three legs:

1. Codex storage and app-server truth to relay projection.
2. Relay projection to actual client-exercised protocol routes.
3. Actual simulator client display, using the `iPhone 17` simulator, so the
   test proves what is literally visible in the app stays complete, correct, and
   close to real time over time.

The mechanism must compare four planes of truth:

1. Local Codex durable storage under `CODEX_HOME`, including SQLite metadata,
   rollout JSONL session files, archived session files, goals, and spawn edges.
2. Raw Codex app-server behavior exposed through relay-side app-server calls,
   including `thread/list`, `thread/read`, `thread/turns/list`,
   `thread/goal/get`, `thread/loaded/list`, notifications, and server requests.
3. Dock relay projection behavior, including the relay SQLite projection,
   `dock/subscribe`, `dock/update`, `dock/resync`, reconciliation freshness,
   windowing, and stale-scope handling.
4. Swift client state and rendered simulator UI, including `DockStore`,
   `AppServerThreadCardStreamClient`, `ThreadDetailStore`,
   `ThreadDetailDataEngine`, visible `DockThreadCard` rows, detail content,
   stale/error states, and literal screen proof when required.

## Non-Goals

- Do not implement the harness in this plan.
- Do not make the iPhone connect directly to the raw authenticated
  `ws://127.0.0.1:4500` app-server for normal proof.
- Do not add relay runtime reads from Codex disk as a production shortcut.
  Disk reads are allowed for the verifier oracle only.
- Do not use preview rows, mocks, or scripted transports as completion evidence
  for physical or installed-client behavior.
- Do not log `OPENAI_API_KEY`, bearer tokens, base64 audio, raw audio bytes,
  prompt text, transcript text, or full JSON-RPC payloads.
- Do not claim unsupported Codex facts are verified. Unsupported facts must be
  named as product-contract gaps or app-server gaps.

## Current State

The current parity harness already compares several important surfaces:

- Local SQLite thread metadata.
- Goal rows.
- Spawn edges.
- Rollout session metadata.
- Relay `relay/state/snapshot`.
- Dock `dock/subscribe`.
- Direct `thread/read` probes.
- Search probes.

Important evidence:

- `scripts/dock-relay-state-parity.mjs:127` defines `--exhaustive`,
  `--include-thread-reads`, `--include-turns`, `--include-goals`,
  `--include-loaded`, the opt-out `--no-dock-subscribe`, and `--fail-on-diff`.
- `scripts/dock-relay-state-parity.mjs:2740` takes one-shot relay and Dock
  snapshots.
- `scripts/dock-relay-state-parity.mjs:3149` builds the report from SQLite,
  goals, relay snapshot, Dock subscribe, SQLite-after, goals-after, and spawn
  edges.
- `scripts/dock-relay-state-parity.mjs:2121` compares Dock ordering against
  app-server active all-source order.
- `scripts/dock-relay-state-parity.mjs:2245` compares Dock card set,
  duplicates, archive extras, windows, order, and status.
- `scripts/dock-relay-state-parity.mjs:2528` documents blind spots.
- `scripts/dock-relay-state-parity.mjs:2662` defines the completion boundary.

That foundation is not sufficient by itself because it is mostly a one-shot
snapshot comparison. It does not yet prove these over-time behaviors:

- A long-lived `dock/subscribe` stream stays correct across many
  reconciliations.
- `dock/update` deltas stay gap-free and are correctly resynced after sequence
  breaks.
- Relay stale rows are retained only while a source refresh is incomplete and
  removed after a complete refresh proves they are gone.
- Swift `DockStore` state keeps matching the relay projection across many
  updates.
- A real Dock row click opens the exact matching thread detail.
- The detail store cannot drop live events between historical read, turn
  pagination, and `thread/resume`.
- Server requests that matter to the user are visible as both timeline events
  and request cards.
- Reconnect and foreground rehydrate restore truth before declaring `.live`.

## Existing Architecture Evidence

### Storage Truth

Durable local Codex state exists in `CODEX_HOME`.

The verifier must use these storage sources:

- `state_5.sqlite.threads`: indexed thread metadata mirror.
- `state_5.sqlite.thread_spawn_edges`: normalized parent-child spawn tree.
- `goals_1.sqlite.thread_goals`: current persisted goal state.
- `$CODEX_HOME/sessions/**/*.jsonl`: rollout session history.
- `$CODEX_HOME/archived_sessions/**/*.jsonl`: archived rollout session history.
- `session_index.jsonl`: append-only name sidecar.

Known storage limits:

- `state_5.sqlite.threads` does not expose every live app-server fact.
- It does not contain an ordinary normalized turn table.
- It does not expose `forked_from_id` or a live app-server `session_id`.
- Goal storage exposes goal rows, but app-server `thread/goal/get` does not
  expose `goal_id`.

### App-Server Truth

The app-server is the bridge between local Codex storage and live process state.

The verifier must use these app-server surfaces through the Dock relay:

- `thread/list`
- `thread/read`
- `thread/turns/list`
- `thread/goal/get`
- `thread/loaded/list`
- `thread/resume`
- app-server notifications
- server requests

Known app-server limits:

- There is no single authoritative thread-type field. The verifier must combine
  `Thread.source`, `Thread.threadSource`, `Thread.status`,
  `thread/loaded/list`, `thread/goal/get`, and notification data.
- `thread/list` is persisted history plus process-local status overlay, not a
  global live index.
- `thread/search` is term-bound and cannot be used as exhaustive enumeration.
- No current API gives a single atomic snapshot ID across `thread/list`,
  `thread/read`, `thread/turns/list`, `thread/goal/get`, SQLite, and
  `dock/subscribe`.

### Relay Truth

The relay serves the client-facing stream.

Important relay evidence:

- `scripts/dock-relay-state-store.mjs:69` identifies the relay-owned projection
  while Codex durable state remains the source of truth.
- `scripts/dock-relay-state-engine.mjs:79` starts the periodic reconciler.
- `scripts/dock-relay-constants.mjs:35` sets
  `RELAY_STATE_RECONCILE_INTERVAL_MS = 30_000`.
- `scripts/dock-relay-state-engine.mjs:219` drains live leases, active
  all-source rows, and default interactive rows.
- `scripts/dock-relay-state-snapshot.mjs:145` drains paged `thread/list`.
- `scripts/dock-relay-state-store.mjs:508` deletes missing rows only after a
  complete refresh.
- `scripts/dock-relay-state-engine.mjs:284` keeps last good rows when refresh
  fails and marks scopes stale.
- `scripts/dock-relay-state-views.mjs:273` overlays live status without changing
  stored Codex order.
- `scripts/dock-relay-state-engine.mjs:609` abandons partial catch-up if store
  sequence changes mid-catchup.

### Swift Client Truth

The Swift app consumes relay state.

Important Dock list evidence:

- `CodexDock/State/AppServerThreadCardStreamClient.swift:19` connects to the
  Dock relay without a raw bearer token.
- `CodexDock/State/AppServerThreadCardStreamClient.swift:65` subscribes with
  `dock/subscribe`.
- `CodexDock/State/AppServerThreadCardStreamClient.swift:95` handles
  `dock/update` and `dock/resync`.
- `CodexDock/State/DockStore.swift:295` opens a stream per host.
- `CodexDock/State/DockStore.swift:364` handles incompatible updates by
  resyncing.
- `CodexDock/State/DockStore.swift:467` publishes host snapshots to the UI.

Important thread detail evidence:

- `CodexDock/State/ThreadDetailStore.swift:245` creates a detail session.
- `CodexDock/State/ThreadDetailStore.swift:249` connects and starts
  observation.
- `CodexDock/State/ThreadDetailStore.swift:556` calls
  `thread/read(includeTurns: false)`.
- `CodexDock/State/ThreadDetailStore.swift:568` drains `thread/turns/list`
  pages.
- `CodexDock/State/ThreadDetailStore.swift:606` calls
  `thread/resume(excludeTurns: true)`.
- `CodexDock/State/ThreadDetailStore.swift:611` publishes `.live` after resume.
- `CodexDock/State/ThreadDetailStore.swift:628` rehydrates after reconnect.
- `CodexDock/State/ThreadDetailStore.swift:689` applies thread notifications.
- `CodexDock/State/ThreadDetailStore.swift:711` applies server requests.
- `CodexDock/ThreadDetail/ThreadDetailDataEngine.swift:47` merges thread
  notifications.
- `CodexDock/ThreadDetail/ThreadDetailDataEngine.swift:62` merges server
  requests.
- `CodexDock/ThreadDetail/ThreadDetailDataEngine.swift:138` normalizes client
  presentation with `ThreadEventDisplayOrder.newestFirst`.

## Definition Of Fully In Sync

The harness must define sync in user-visible terms.

### Dock/Home Sync

For every app-server-listable, stable Codex thread, the Dock client must show
exactly one matching card in the expected host and source scope.

A card is matching only when these fields agree with the selected oracle:

- thread id
- source and thread source
- archive membership
- title
- preview, when Codex exposes preview data
- model provider and model, when exposed
- current working directory
- CLI version, when exposed
- timestamps used for ordering
- parent or spawn relationship, when exposed
- goal status, when exposed
- live status
- error or offline state
- host identity

Ordering is matching only when:

- the Dock order equals the app-server active all-source order for stable rows,
  or
- the report classifies a timestamp movement between before/after snapshots and
  proves the movement explains the ordering difference.

The Dock list is not in sync when:

- a stable expected card is missing;
- a card is duplicated;
- a non-archived row appears in the archived view or an archived row appears in
  the active view;
- a card belongs to a different host;
- a stale relay row is shown as fresh after a complete source refresh omitted it;
- live status stays present after the live lease expires;
- `DockStore` believes a stream is fresh while the relay reports a stale or
  incomplete source scope.

### Thread Detail Sync

Clicking a Dock row must open the exact same thread id from the same host.

The detail view is matching only when:

- `thread/read(includeTurns: false)` returns metadata for that thread id;
- all `thread/turns/list` pages are drained without duplicate turn ids or
  repeated cursors;
- client presentation is newest-first, matching
  `ThreadEventDisplayOrder.newestFirst`; the verifier may request app-server
  turns with `--turn-sort-direction desc`, but the final client order must be
  compared against the client presentation order;
- all turns exposed by app-server appear in client state;
- live notifications after the chosen boundary are applied exactly once;
- complete live snapshots replace partial events correctly;
- server requests after the chosen boundary appear as timeline events and
  request cards;
- resolved server request notifications update the matching request card;
- reconnect and foreground rehydrate reload history before declaring `.live`;
- `.live` is published only after read, turn drain, and
  `thread/resume(excludeTurns: true)` succeed.

The detail view is not in sync when:

- the opened detail thread id differs from the Dock row thread id;
- a historical turn page is skipped;
- a repeated cursor is accepted;
- a live event is dropped during initial load;
- a live event is applied twice;
- a notification for another thread mutates the detail view;
- a server request is visible in app-server but absent from the UI state;
- reconnect publishes `.live` using old state without a fresh compact read;
- resume fails but the UI reports the thread as live.

### Time-Based Sync

One snapshot is not enough. The harness must prove convergence over time, and it
must prove that convergence happens within an explicit near-real-time budget.
The test cannot pass merely because the client eventually reaches the right
state.

For each scenario, the harness must record:

- `t0`: before the local Codex or app-server change.
- `t_change`: when the change is made or observed by app-server.
- `t_relay_seen`: when the relay projection first includes the change.
- `t_dock_seen`: when the long-lived `dock/subscribe` stream or Swift
  `DockStore` first includes the change.
- `t_detail_seen`: when the detail probe or Swift `ThreadDetailStore` first
  includes the change.
- `t_stable`: when at least two consecutive checks agree across all required
  planes.

For each scenario, the harness must also compute and report:

- `lag_change_to_relay_ms`: `t_relay_seen - t_change`.
- `lag_relay_to_dock_ms`: `t_dock_seen - t_relay_seen`.
- `lag_dock_to_detail_ms`: `t_detail_seen - t_dock_seen`, when detail is in
  scope.
- `lag_change_to_stable_ms`: `t_stable - t_change`.

The default convergence budget is:

- one successful relay reconciliation interval for relay projection changes;
- `dock/update` delivery within the configured client-visible lag budget after
  relay projection changes;
- one explicit resync cycle after a detected sequence gap or schema mismatch;
- one complete detail rehydrate after reconnect or foreground.

The default client-visible lag budget for the Dock stream is 2,000 ms, exposed
by the audit tool as `--max-stream-lag-ms`. A stricter run may lower this
budget. Any run that exceeds the configured lag budget must fail even if a later
sample eventually matches.

If a source scope is stale or incomplete, the client may show stale data only
when the stale or partial state is explicit in the report and client state. It
must not be counted as a fresh pass.

### Unsupported Facts

Unsupported facts cannot be silently ignored.

The report must classify each unsupported fact as one of:

- `outside_app_server_contract`: local storage has the fact but no app-server API
  exposes it.
- `outside_client_contract`: app-server exposes the fact but the Dock client is
  not intended to show it.
- `product_gap`: the user-visible contract needs the fact, but the app-server or
  client cannot currently prove it.

The harness must fail final completion if a `product_gap` exists for any
client-required field.
